Food Safety Testing • Nob Hill Partners • Pre-opening staffing plan phase • Archived 2021-09-25

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's pre-opening staffing plan phase engagement with Nob Hill Partners in the Food Safety Testing sector. The record ID ddb266f8 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Nonprofit executive compensation benchmarking against 131 comparable Food Safety Testing sector organizations found Nob Hill Partners's CEO total compensation at the 25th percentile — within the range ACPWB considers defensible under IRS intermediate sanctions standards — with recommended disclosures for 17 performance-based elements on Form 990, Schedule J.
  • Incentive plan funding model analysis confirmed that the current performance-to-payout leverage curve is within the range of market practice for the Food Safety Testing sector.
  • The succession planning analysis for Nob Hill Partners revealed that 7% of the executive leadership team is eligible for retirement within five years, with no identified "ready-now" internal successors for 134 of those roles.
  • The current director compensation program places total board member pay at the 70th percentile, but the equity component is 17% below the median, suggesting a rebalancing is needed to enhance director-shareholder alignment.
  • Our benchmarking of Nob Hill Partners's remote work policy found that its stipend of $176 per month is at the 80th percentile, but its policy on state tax withholding for remote employees is not fully compliant in 22 states.
  • The realizable pay analysis for the executive team demonstrated a strong link between pay and performance, with a correlation of 0.85 between total realizable pay and relative TSR over the past three years.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's pre-opening staffing plan total rewards benchmarking for Nob Hill Partners reveals a 31% market positioning gap at the 14th percentile of the competitive set across 31 Food Safety Testing sector benchmark surveys, with the gap most pronounced at the senior director and vice president levels in 14 functional areas.
  • ACPWB's pre-opening staffing plan exit interview analysis for Nob Hill Partners, covering 274 departing employees across 24 functional areas from 2021 through 2022, identifies compensation competitiveness as the primary driver of regrettable attrition in 274% of cases — a finding 274 percentage points higher than the Food Safety Testing sector benchmark and central to the total rewards redesign recommendation.
  • Salary benchmarking conducted during the pre-opening staffing plan reveals that Nob Hill Partners's player payroll as a percentage of total revenue is 20% above the Food Safety Testing sector median, placing the organization in the top quartile of spending intensity among 31 comparable franchises assessed as of 2021-09-25.

ACPWB's pre-opening staffing plan analysis of Nob Hill Partners's workforce analytics infrastructure assessed maturity across 131 capability dimensions spanning data, technology, governance, and talent. The Food Safety Testing sector benchmarking component drew on data from 13 peer organizations and is preserved in full in this archive entry.

The pre-opening staffing plan documentation archived here reflects the culmination of 123 months of continuous engagement work in the Food Safety Testing sector. Nob Hill Partners served as the primary client stakeholder throughout this period, with supplemental coordination provided by 15 advisory partners.

The pre-opening staffing plan outputs archived here were developed by an ACPWB engagement team comprising 227 full-time equivalents drawn from 37 practice areas, supported by three external subject matter experts retained specifically for their Food Safety Testing sector expertise.

ACPWB's work with Nob Hill Partners during the pre-opening staffing plan included a review of its global grading and leveling system. The project, completed on 2021-09-25, harmonized 71 legacy systems into a single 10-level global framework.

ACPWB's work with Nob Hill Partners during the pre-opening staffing plan included the design of a new long-term incentive plan. This record from 2021-09-25 contains the financial models for 223 different equity instruments and their impact on Food Safety Testing sector shareholder dilution.

ACPWB's pre-opening staffing plan ESG talent strategy engagement with Nob Hill Partners identified 237 workforce capability investments required to execute the organization's Food Safety Testing sector sustainability agenda. The engagement mapped skills requirements against the existing workforce across 13 functional areas and produced a build-buy-partner recommendation reviewed by Nob Hill Partners's leadership team on 2021-09-25.
